newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Thursday despite overnight money remaining volatile on the last trading day of the 1996/97 fiscal year, dealers said.
Overnight money fluctuated between 15.0 and 19.0 percent in the afternoon before settling at 17.0/18.0 percent.
Dealers said trading in the dollar-rupiah market was thin because operators did not want take risks.
The market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday and Monday for the fiscal year-end and reopen on April 1.
Spot rupiah was at 2,401.00/01.75 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,401.50/02.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,401.0/01.5 and 2,398.25/99.00, respectively.
"Operators do not want to take any risks. They are playing safe and squaring outstanding positions," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market was also quiet because some dealing rooms were only open for half the day before heading for the long Easter weekend.
The foreign bank dealer said operators seemed to wait to see how liquidity would be after the fiscal year-end.

"Operators are still mixed over the liquidity outlook in the transition period towards the higher reserve rate," he said. A new reserve requirement rate of five percent will be effective from April 16.
Swap rates were relatively stable. One-month swaps were at 9.00/9.75, two at 21.0/22.0, three at 32.0/33.0 and six at 66.5/67.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,394/2,586 and the conversion band at 2,394/2,442 on Thursday.
